subject: PII handling for prompts/outputs — post-call follow-up
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 16:00:00 -0700
Subject: PII handling for prompts/outputs — post-call follow-up

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call today. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize how Redwood handles customer prompts and model outputs (what we store, where, and retention), and list next steps. Please let me know any clarifying questions; I'm happy to loop legal or our privacy engineer (Neha).

Recap (high level):
- Default hosted API behavior: prompts and outputs (request/response payloads) are logged for operational troubleshooting and rate-limiting purposes. By default, we retain these logs for 30 days.
- Training: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts or outputs to train our public models. We may use anonymized telemetry at aggregate levels for performance/quality metrics unless the customer opts out.
- Data residency: Hosted API logs are stored in the region you choose (us/eu/apac). For customers requiring strict residency, Dedicated or Private deployments keep all logs inside customer-controlled infrastructure.
- Access controls: Only authorized Redwood engineers (support on a case-by-case ACL) can access logs; access is audited and tied to support tickets.
- Configurations: Customers can disable request/response logging in Hosted under an Enterprise agreement, or choose Dedicated/Private to prevent storage in Redwood-managed systems.

Attached is a short one-pager with the above and links to our docs and SOC2 evidence.

Next steps:
1) Sam to confirm whether Acme needs default Hosted with logging disabled or Dedicated/Private deployment.
2) If Hosted but logging disabled, Legal to confirm contractual language for non-retention.
3) If Dedicated/Private, schedule tech session with Neha to map network/KMS requirements.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: redwood-pii-handling-summary.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmecorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PII handling for prompts/outputs — post-call follow-up

Thanks Rishi — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications before I take this to our Security & Legal teams:
1) When you say "retain logs for 30 days" — does that include full prompt text and model output (i.e., customer payloads), or are those redacted?
2) Who exactly can access the logs at Redwood (roles/title)? Can you provide an audit trail example?
3) For Hosted customers that opt out of logging, is there an option to still capture minimal telemetry (errors/latency) without storing raw payloads?

Also, can you confirm whether Redwood ever stores derived embeddings or vectorized representations of prompts/outputs? That's a blocker for us.

Appreciate a short bullet answer we can forward to Legal.

Sam
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Corp

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmecorp.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PII handling for prompts/outputs — post-call follow-up

Hi Sam — quick bullets for Legal (copied Neha for technical confirmation):
- Retention: Default hosted logs include full request and response payloads and are retained for 30 days. Those records are accessible only to a small set of authorized engineers and support staff under strict IAM and are audited.
- Redaction: We can enable payload redaction for Hosted customers (Enterprise add-on) which strips fields or masks patterns before storage.
- Minimal telemetry: Yes — customers can opt to keep only non-payload telemetry (error rates, latency, request sizes) while disabling payload logs. This is a common configuration and preserves observability without storing text.
- Embeddings: Redwood does NOT automatically store derived embeddings or vectorized representations for Hosted customers. If a customer explicitly opts into vector store hosting (e.g., Redwood-managed embeddings storage), that is a separate product and retention is configurable.
- Residency & Dedicated/Private: For strict residency or zero-Redwood-storage requirements, Dedicated or Private deployments ensure data never leaves the customer's tenancy. KMS/HSM integration available for key control.
- Audit trail: All accesses to logs are logged with user, timestamp, and ticket reference. Neha can share a redacted sample audit extract and our SOC2 procedures.

If helpful, Neha can join a short call with your Security team to walk through the SOC2 artifacts and KMS options.

Best,
Rishi

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmecorp.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: PII handling for prompts/outputs — post-call follow-up

Hi Sam — adding the technical confirmations you asked for and a pointer to evidence. Short answers for Legal: 
- Full payloads: Yes, by default hosted logs include full request/response payloads retained for 30 days. We can provide a contract amendment to limit retention or enable payload redaction.
- Access: Access is role-based and requires approval; typical roles with access are Support Engineers, SREs, and a scoped Security Ops group. Each access event is recorded (user, timestamp, ticket ID, purpose).
- Audit sample: Attached is a redacted audit extract and a link to our SOC2 guidance.
- Embeddings: We do not persist embeddings unless you explicitly use our Managed Embeddings product. If you plan to use embeddings, we recommend Dedicated/Private with customer-controlled storage and KMS.

Documents attached: redwood-pii-handling-summary.pdf; SOC2 evidence redirect link.

Happy to schedule the security deep-dive — propose Wed 11/04 or Thu 11/05.

Thanks,
